video_generation_spec.title: Superfast Earth Precession Movement and Synchronized Sinusoidal Graph

reproducibility.style: 3D scientific animation with integrated 2D dynamic vector overlays
reproducibility.lighting: Realistic directional sunlight from off-screen left against deep space

scene_layout.background: Deep black space canvas featuring subtle distant starfields and faint nebula dust

left_zone.position: Left third of the frame (x: 15% to 35%, y: 50%)
features: Photorealistic 3D Earth surface with continents and ocean shading
Superfast axial rotation along its own geographic axis (spinning like a top)
Rapid, continuous orbital wobble around the central precession axis (many complete cycles)
NO axis lines, NO elevation lines, and NO text/numerical overlays on or along the Earth

right_zone.position: Right two-thirds of the frame (x: 35% to 95%, y: 20% to 80%)
right_zone.line_drawing_direction: Glowing cyan sine wave constructed dynamically from right to left, extending and shading smoothly towards the Earth

inset_overlay.position: Top-right corner inset box (x: 75% to 92%, y: 10% to 35%)
inset_overlay.style: Semi-transparent rectangular frame with subtle border glow
inset_overlay.motion: Classic toy top spinning at ultra-high speed while wobbling gyroscopically to visually explain axial precession physics

timeline.action: Deep space canvas initializes. The photorealistic 3D Earth appears on the left, spinning superfast along its axis. Graph coordinate axes appear on the right with sin(θ) labels.

Earth continues its ultra-fast daily rotation while executing multiple rapid gyroscopic revolutions around the precession wobble path. On the right, a glowing cyan sin(θ) wave begins plotting from right to left toward Earth.

A semi-transparent inset window pops up in the top-right corner featuring a toy top spinning and wobbling rapidly. Earth continues fast multi-round precession loops on the left while the sine wave extends further toward the globe.

The sin(θ) curve completes its path near Earth with subtle area-under-the-curve shading. The spinning top inset window smoothly fades out as Earth maintains its fast daily spin and rapid orbital wobble cycles.

video_generation_spec.text_prompt_for_ai: High-fidelity 16:9 3D scientific animation with 200px render height against a deep space background. On the left third, realistic 3D Earth spinning superfast on its own axis while making many rapid circular revolutions around its precession wobble path (clean Earth surface with NO axis lines or numbers). On the right two-thirds, a scientific graph rendering a glowing cyan sin(theta) wave from right to left toward Earth. In the top-right corner, an inset overlay showing a fast-wobbling toy top demonstrating gyroscopic precession physics. Smooth 30fps animation.
